finding: The final coverage checks show every line of both notices reachable in overlapping scroll positions on both runtimes. Whole-screen native audits still fail and retain their unassociated contrast/clipping reports. Reachability does not explain or waive those reports.
retainedHarnessFailures: First test jumped between start/end positions and left a middle coverage gap; its attempted whole-paragraph positioning also oscillated with native search chrome.

Second test covered all segments reached but made a trailing StaticText query after its node disappeared; the locator now follows any accessibility element with the exact wording, and final comparison uses the captured initial height.

First iOS 27 run failed three end-height comparisons at floating-point differences near 1e-13 points. Final coverage uses a 0.001-point precision allowance; no accessibility audit type, handler or contrast threshold changed.

Initial result export lacked permission for the Xcode cache; the authorized export succeeded. Initial simulator cleanup found one device already shut down; state-aware cleanup preserves unrelated simulators.
limitations: The audit does not identify which SwiftUI nodes produced the retained reports. No blanket scroll-edge or inactive-control waiver is asserted.
The tests use synthetic sample data and do not request Contacts permission, edit the address book, call a phone, send messages or activate caretaker delivery.
The original unfiltered failure bundles remain available. Simulator reachability does not verify physical VoiceOver gestures, complete spoken output or full accessibility.

Production source is unchanged from the 256-input verified unsigned contact-recovery archive. No archive was rebuilt for this test-only follow-up. Backend checks are referenced from the unchanged passing source checkpoint, not newly claimed.
